### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea6de745cce19d0de551e938a6fc6bbe975dd35e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3e87d87c9ac151830df94d3ed3db1ee2fed4ed04` — the merge of head `d2aa1132d3d45688ee1604ae421443028e013c3e` into base `ea6de745cce19d0de551e938a6fc6bbe975dd35e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3e87d87c9ac151830df94d3ed3db1ee2fed4ed04 && git checkout 3e87d87c9ac151830df94d3ed3db1ee2fed4ed04
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ea6de745cce19d0de551e938a6fc6bbe975dd35e d2aa1132d3d45688ee1604ae421443028e013c3e && git checkout -B drift-repro ea6de745cce19d0de551e938a6fc6bbe975dd35e && git merge --no-ff d2aa1132d3d45688ee1604ae421443028e013c3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ea6de745cce19d0de551e938a6fc6bbe975dd35e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `d2aa1132d3d45688ee1604ae421443028e013c3e`
Reviewer: review-c · read 2026-11-15T23:18Z · ordinary ACCEPT read (`review-checklist.md`); no contract face, so no contract record is owed
Implemented-by: `claude/area-E1b-33832` (area S5) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jRMKz5NhWVrE4E1U5x

- **The card's step 1 came first.** Reach was measured on a real boot: 8 boots, both registration orders, with and without DB hydration. The card's exact no-composite shape does not form, but its mechanism does: tier 2 registers the service's last-registered pick in the bare slot. Taking the fix route for the mechanism is right, and the body records the unreachable symptom rather than filing it.
- **The guard is exact.** It fires only for a package-addressed type (`isPackageScopedType`) that the store keeps by name alone (outside `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES`), and only when the registry holds the name for two or more packages, disabled ones counted. There it returns a settled miss before any service read. Tier 3 still retires only the removed row's own entry. A name one package holds, and the package-slotted types, read as before.
- **Counting disabled holders is right.** With one holder disabled, the service's single item may be the disabled package's body. Registering it bare would serve a disabled package's item; the empty slot leaves the answer to the registry's holder rules.
- **`Clause-②: no` is right.** The PR restores the post-heal state to what boot already answers: the bare slot is empty, and a bare read gets the refusal naming every holder. It also drops the duplicate listing. The pick existed only between a delete and the next boot and was never a steady-state answer, so no accept set moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` and the `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` are right, and the changeset text is true of the diff.
- **The pins bite.** One new describe sits in the shared real-registry heal harness (real `SchemaRegistry` and `MetadataManager`, the real boot's composite-slot shape), covering `dashboard` and `report`. The ablation went through `dist/`, with preflight markers present and then absent; the restore matches HEAD, 12 of 12.
- **Checks:** all 51 check-runs passed or were skipped, none red; `mergeable_state: clean`.

No must-fix, no should-fix. Not governed: the area lands this PR per `landing-operations.md`.
